A hospital manager believes the number of people arriving at the emergency room for work-related incidents has increased in the last year. Last year, an average of $0.5$ people per day arrived at the emergency room for work-related incidents. Let $X$ represent the number of people arriving at the emergency room for work-related incidents in a one-day period. Under the null hypothesis that the number of people is the same as before, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $10%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **probability mass function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis. You may assume that, under the null hypothesis, $P(X \ge 6) = 0$.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X = x)$ | $0.6065$ | $0.3033$ | $0.0758$ | $0.0126$ | $0.0016$ | $0.0002$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.

A magician has a $6$-sided die, and an audience member suspects it is biased towards landing on $1$. Let $X$ represent the number of times the die lands on $1$ when rolled a total of $5$ times. Under the null hypothesis that the die is fair, what is the critical region of a one-tailed test at a significance level of $5%$?

*Hint: You may use the table below, representing the **probability mass function** of $X$ under the null hypothesis.*

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| $P(X = x)$ | $0.4019$ | $0.4019$ | $0.1608$ | $0.0322$ | $0.0032$ | $0.0001$ |

> A scientific calculator is required to answer this question.
